title: Adaptive micro-sparkline with semantic focus ring and incremental virtualized summaries
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Dashboard pages render hundreds of tiny KPI sparklines. Current implementation uses DOM-heavy SVG instances and generic tooltips which creates high CPU usage, a11y gaps for screen reader users, and inconsistent focus treatment across keyboard navigation. Scope: design a single reusable micro-sparkline component that supports a low-power canvas fallback, semantic focus ring for keyboard/assistive-tech, incremental virtualized summarization for offscreen series, and token-driven color/contrast profiles so teams can opt into compact sparklines without custom CSS. Deliverables: detailed component spec, token proposal for three density modes, accessibility guidance (ARIA roles, live region summaries), interaction states, and implementation handoff notes for engineers including two perf budgets (mobile/desktop).
acceptance_criteria: New micro-sparkline component spec exists in the design system with examples for 1, 3, and 7 datapoint variants
Color and density tokens proposed and linked to DS token registry
Keyboard focus ring behavior documented and validated against WCAG focus contrast guidelines
Canvas fallback path described with thresholds when to switch from SVG -> canvas to reduce main-thread work
Prototype shows at least 35% CPU improvement in synthetic dashboard with 200 sparklines vs current implementation
Screen-reader summary mode implemented via aria-hidden + aria-live text for the active/offscreen region and accepted by accessibility review
comments: 2025-02-21 Maya Chen: Initial discovery — collected live dashboard telemetry (avg 180 sparklines per page). Noted spikes in main-thread during route change. Added perf profiling docs and sample traces to the ticket.

2025-02-24 Arjun Patel: Spike triage — profiled SVG rendering cost. Suggest canvas fallback when pointCount > 12 or when rendering more than 50 instances in the viewport. Also recommended batching style updates to reduce layout thrashing.
2025-02-26 Design critique: Accessibility-first approach accepted. Action: add two screen-reader patterns (verbose aria-live summary and concise label-only mode) and test with NVDA/VoiceOver.

2025-03-01 Engineering review (Lucas Rivera): Raised question about KV cache interactions for time-aligned sparklines. Proposed solution: share precomputed min/max/last-value metadata from the runtime to avoid per-component scans.
2025-03-03 PM sync (Nora Blake): Suggested shipping token set in next console release and gating animation by a feature flag for rapid rollback if perf regressions appear.
2025-03-04 Arjun Patel: Prototype completed — attached perf numbers and screencasts. Filed PR for canvas fallback and token additions. See PR and figma links below.
perf_metrics: Baseline (current SVG): median main-thread CPU 420ms/frame when mounting 200 sparklines
Prototype (canvas + virtualization): median main-thread CPU 270ms/frame — ~36% improvement
Memory overhead: canvas fallback increased heap by ~8MB for 200 sparklines but reduced layout recalculations
Interaction latency: keyboard focus moves to sparkline within 16ms on modern desktop when using precomputed metadata
decisions: Use canvas fallback for density > 50 instances in a continuous viewport or per-sparkline pointCount > 12
Expose three density tokens: sparkline-density-compact, sparkline-density-regular, sparkline-density-relaxed
Provide two a11y modes: 'narrative' (aria-live summaries) and 'label-only' (concise aria-label); default to label-only
Default focus ring uses semantic token border-focus-strong with 3px offset to satisfy contrast when zoomed
Animations should be disabled by default on low-power devices and behind a feature flag for initial rollout
